question.text: Per the current NISM XVII workbook, how are gains on a specified mutual fund (e.g., a debt-oriented fund investing 65% or more in debt) acquired on or after April 1, 2023 taxed?

answer.text: Long-term capital gains at 20% with indexation if held more than 36 months
Long-term capital gains at 12.5% if held more than 12 months
Gains are taxed at applicable / marginal slab rates as short-term capital gains, irrespective of holding period
Exempt up to Rs. 1 lakh per financial year and 10% beyond, similar to equity LTCG

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the current NISM XVII workbook (pp.180, 204), gains on a specified mutual fund (investing 65% or more in debt) acquired on or after April 1, 2023 are taxed at applicable/marginal slab rates as short-term capital gains, irrespective of holding period. The legacy 36-month LTCG-with-indexation regime for debt mutual funds is no longer applicable for such acquisitions. The Trap: 36 months with indexation reflects the legacy rule; 12.5% above Rs. 1 lakh is the equity LTCG regime, not debt; and there is no equity-style Rs. 1 lakh exemption for debt-fund gains. Cross-Exam Context: NISM XVII, V-A, and X-B all test the post-April-1-2023 specified-mutual-fund taxation regime in retirement-planning, distribution-product, and tax chapters.
